clue.text: Saw dog's name inside lead

indicators.note: inside says the dog's name is placed within the letters for lead

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for the metal lead
Rover is the stock name for a pet dog

explanation.surface: A dog's name tag sits inside the loop of its lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of 'see' or a cutting tool, but here it is the noun for an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, the same thing as a familiar adage.

clue.text: Turn up in chilly setting yet well received

indicators.note: setting means the chilly word surrounds the other letters like a mount around a gem

parts.note: polar means extremely cold

indicators.note: Turn says the little word is flipped round

explanation.surface: Turning up somewhere cold, a visitor is still warmly welcomed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something popular is liked by many, widely well received.

clue.text: They give people their addresses

parts.note: addresses reads as where people live but means speeches given to an audience

explanation.definitionFit: Public speakers deliver speeches, also called addresses, to audiences.

clue.text: Something fragrant returned in the time left

indicators.note: returned means the letters are read from right to left
in says the letters lie within the phrase

explanation.surface: The clock shows the time remaining for a perfumer's task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned in' signals a backwards hidden word: read 'the time left' right to left to find it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant resin used in perfumes and varnishes.

clue.text: Unhappy with split in state of Kentucky?

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling unhappy
to split on someone is to inform, or grass, on them

explanation.surface: A gloomy man splits up while living in Kentucky.
explanation.walkthrough: Kentucky's nickname is the Bluegrass State, so the question mark signals a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Kentucky is nicknamed the Bluegrass State after the meadow grass growing there.

clue.text: The sound of seals or swans

indicators.note: the sound of says a word is to be pronounced, then spelt differently

parts.note: signets are seals, small engraved stamps set in rings

explanation.surface: A naturalist compares the cries of seals with those of swans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seals' suggests the animals, but it means signet rings; the word for them is said aloud to give young swans.
explanation.definitionFit: Cygnets are young swans, so they are swans of a kind.

clue.text: Embrace son during thunderburst

indicators.note: during says the letter for son comes in the middle of the thunder

parts.note: a clap of thunder is a sudden burst

explanation.surface: A mother hugs her boy tight during a thunderstorm.
explanation.definitionFit: To clasp someone is to hold them tight, an embrace.

clue.text: Soldiers possibly armed with guns

indicators.note: possibly suggests another arrangement of the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Troops may well carry weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Guardsmen are soldiers of a regiment of guards.

clue.text: Do some spelling, can then be qualified

indicators.note: be qualified means be modified or altered, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: A good speller can then gain a qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spelling' suggests writing words correctly, but it means casting spells.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant is to put under a spell, literally to work some magic.

clue.text: Bent lawyer retiring to rest, perhaps

parts.note: retiring means shy and modest

indicators.note: perhaps hints the word may appear in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A crooked solicitor withdraws to take a rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A shyster is an unscrupulous, dishonest lawyer; bent is slang for corrupt.

clue.text: Paul brewed tea in a high-rise flat

indicators.note: brewed means mixed and stewed, so the letters of the two words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Paul makes a pot of tea in his tower-block apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-rise flat' reads as a tower-block apartment but means an area of flat land standing high up.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is an expanse of level ground at altitude, literally flat land that rises high.

clue.text: Chief is in some confusion

indicators.note: is in says the word for chief sits inside the word for some

parts.note: any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'
arch as an adjective means chief or principal, as in arch-enemy

explanation.surface: The leader of the group is himself rather bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchy is a state of lawless disorder, total confusion with nobody in control.

clue.text: Improving by using a reference book?

definitions.meaning: a situation that is getting better is said to be on the up
consulting a dictionary to find a word is looking it up

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means getting better, and also consulting a dictionary or similar source for a word.

clue.text: Draw a cheque?

definitions.meaning: to sketch an outline or plan is to make a preliminary version
a bank order to pay money, a banker's bill

explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary sketch or drawing, and also a written order for payment like a cheque.

clue.text: I take a break outside then take the exam again

indicators.note: outside says the word for taking a break goes around the I

parts.note: to rest is to take a break

explanation.surface: A student pauses briefly before going back to sit the test again.
explanation.definitionFit: To resit is to sit an examination a second time after failing it.

clue.text: Biting ditch insect

parts.note: a trench is a ditch
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An insect in a ditch gives a nasty bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant remarks are incisive and cutting, i.e. biting.

clue.text: School takes two masters in exchange

indicators.note: takes means the word for exchange holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: to alter is to change or exchange one thing for another

indicators.note: two says the abbreviation is written out twice

parts.note: MA is Master of Arts, a master's degree

explanation.surface: A school recruits a pair of teachers in a staff swap.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma mater, Latin for nourishing mother, names the school or college a person attended.

clue.text: A central figure at the trade centre?

definitions.text: A central figure at the trade centre?

parts.words: A central figure at the trade centre?
parts.note: the figure is literally in the middle of a deal, between producer and buyer

explanation.definitionFit: An intermediary trader stands between maker and buyer in commerce.

clue.text: Spoke to a number in uniform

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, so a number
someone in uniform is dressed for duty

explanation.surface: A soldier in uniform addressed a crowd of people.
explanation.definitionFit: To address someone is to speak directly to them, so addressed means talked to.

clue.text: Aims to get a ship round an awkward pier

indicators.note: round says the ship's letters wrap around the others

parts.note: SS is steamship

indicators.note: awkward means the word is jumbled clumsily

explanation.surface: A captain tries to steer a vessel around a badly placed jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspires means aims high, hopes to achieve something.

clue.text: Rebuilding Dundee, an old penny is exposed

indicators.note: Rebuilding says the city's letters are reconstructed in a new order

parts.note: d was the symbol for a penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: Regenerating a Scottish city leaves a coin in plain view.
explanation.walkthrough: Dundee is a city in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Denuded means stripped bare, laid exposed.

clue.text: Drain out the bottom

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plumber empties the drain from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, the very bottom.

clue.text: These clubs need licences

parts.note: the clubs look like nightclubs needing alcohol licences, but they are golf woods that share a name with motorists

explanation.definitionFit: Golfers' longest clubs share their name with motorists, who must hold licences.

clue.text: They take no end of towels

definitions.text: They take no end of towels

parts.words: They take no end of towels
parts.note: no end of reads as lots, but means towels formed into an endless loop hung on a revolving bar

explanation.definitionFit: Roller towels are continuous loops hung on rotating bars, so they have no end.

clue.text: Copper holding back in a state of terror

indicators.note: holding says the policeman's letters contain the others

parts.note: copper is slang for a policeman, abbreviated PC for police constable

indicators.note: back means the two words are read backwards

explanation.surface: A frightened police officer holds back a crowd while terrified himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like the metal Cu, but it is the police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear, a state of terror.

clue.text: Keeps a cash register to stop fiddling

parts.note: to keep something is to hold it
a till is a shop's cash register

explanation.surface: Owning a cash register is a way to stop staff stealing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddling' suggests petty fraud at the till; it means fidgeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep motionless is to stop fidgeting with one's hands or body.

clue.text: Very unpopular form of death

indicators.note: form of says a new shape is made from the word's letters

explanation.surface: A grim kind of death no one wants.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hated is intensely disliked, deeply unpopular.

clue.text: Shoes repaired and disposed of, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is pronounced aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: sold means disposed of by sale

explanation.surface: A cobbler fixes footwear and then sells it on.
explanation.definitionFit: Soled describes shoes fitted with new soles, as by a cobbler mending them.

clue.text: Help back into rave looking very happy

indicators.note: into says the reversed letters go inside the word for rave

parts.note: to rant is to rave wildly

indicators.note: back means the word for help is read in reverse

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: A clubber gets assistance at a rave, beaming with joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiant describes someone glowing with joy, visibly delighted.

clue.text: Doctor to tell stories about dramatist

parts.note: MO is a Medical Officer, an army doctor
to tell stories is to lie
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A physician gossips about a playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière was the great seventeenth-century French comic playwright.

clue.text: Solemn number administered barbiturates

parts.note: sedate means calm and solemn
D is 500 in Roman numerals, so a number

explanation.surface: A grave, serious patient count was given sleeping pills.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone given barbiturates has been sedated, calmed with a drug.

clue.text: They don't like to assume anything

definitions.text: They don't like to assume anything

parts.words: They don't like to assume anything
parts.note: assume reads as presume but also means put on clothing, which naturists prefer not to do

explanation.definitionFit: Naturists go unclothed, so they decline to put on any garment.
